## Load data

```{python}
from IPython.display import display
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

user_pgs_scores = pd.read_csv(
    "/home/frederik/snpster_project/important_ppl/bullino_results/psych_pgs.txt", sep="\t"
)

#get metadata

meta_data = pd.read_excel(
    "/home/frederik/github_projects/SNPster/data pipeline/reporting_module/data/pgs_all_metadata.xlsx", sheet_name="Scores"
)

publications_meta_data = pd.read_excel(
    "/home/frederik/github_projects/SNPster/data pipeline/reporting_module/data/pgs_all_metadata.xlsx", sheet_name="Publications"
)   




display(user_pgs_scores.head())
display(meta_data.head())
display(publications_meta_data.head())

```


## Prepare data


```{python}

#only keep sampleset column != reference

user_pgs_scores = user_pgs_scores[user_pgs_scores["sampleset"] != "reference"]
#remove _hmPOS_GRCh38 in the PGS column value strings

user_pgs_scores["PGS"] = user_pgs_scores["PGS"].str.replace("_hmPOS_GRCh38", "", regex=False)


user_pgs_scores = user_pgs_scores.merge(
    meta_data[["Polygenic Score (PGS) ID", "PGS Name", "Reported Trait", "PGS Publication (PGP) ID"]],
    left_on="PGS",
    right_on="Polygenic Score (PGS) ID",
    how="left"
)


publications_meta_data = publications_meta_data[
    publications_meta_data["PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID"].isin(user_pgs_scores["PGS Publication (PGP) ID"])
]


#join Reported Trait from user_pgs_scores to publications_meta_data on the "PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID" and "PGS Publication (PGP) ID" columns
publications_meta_data = publications_meta_data.merge(
    user_pgs_scores[["PGS Publication (PGP) ID", "Reported Trait"]],
    left_on="PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID",
    right_on="PGS Publication (PGP) ID",
    how="left"
)


```


## Plot



```{python}

import plotly.express as px
fig = px.bar(
    user_pgs_scores,
    x="PGS",
    y="percentile_MostSimilarPop",
    color="Reported Trait",
    title="Percentile of Most Similar Population for Each PGS",
    category_orders={"PGS": user_pgs_scores.sort_values("percentile_MostSimilarPop", ascending=False)["PGS"].tolist()},
    template="plotly_white"
)
fig.show()

```


## table

```{python}

df = publications_meta_data.copy()

#drop Authors, PGS Publication (PGP) ID, and PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID columns (too long / not useful for display)

df = df.drop(columns=["Authors", "PGS Publication (PGP) ID", "PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID"])


# Convert everything to display-friendly strings (avoids weird formatting / NaNs)
df_display = df.fillna("").astype(str)

# Align numeric-looking columns to the right, others left
def is_numeric_col(series: pd.Series) -> bool:
    s = pd.to_numeric(series.replace("", pd.NA), errors="coerce")
    return s.notna().mean() > 0.85  # mostly numeric

col_align = ["right" if is_numeric_col(df[c]) else "left" for c in df.columns]

# Zebra striping
row_colors = ["white" if i % 2 == 0 else "#F7F8FA" for i in range(len(df_display))]

fig = go.Figure(
    data=[
        go.Table(
            columnwidth=[1] * len(df_display.columns),
            header=dict(
                values=[f"<b>{c}</b>" for c in df_display.columns],
                fill_color="#F1F3F5",
                font=dict(color="#111827", size=13, family="Inter, Arial"),
                align="left",
                height=36,
                line_color="#E5E7EB",
            ),
            cells=dict(
                values=[df_display[c].tolist() for c in df_display.columns],
                fill_color=[row_colors],  # zebra stripes across rows
                font=dict(color="#111827", size=12, family="Inter, Arial"),
                align=col_align,
                height=30,
                line_color="#E5E7EB",
            ),
        )
    ]
)

fig.update_layout(
    title=dict(
        text="Publications Metadata",
        x=0,
        xanchor="left",
        font=dict(size=18, family="Inter, Arial", color="#111827"),
    ),
    paper_bgcolor="white",
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=55, b=0),
    height=min(850, 140 + 28 * (len(df_display) + 1)),  # auto-ish height
)

fig.show()
```
